content: Emu oil is an oil derived from the refined fat of the emu, a bird native to Australia. It has been utilized for over 1,000 years by Australian Aboriginal people for the treatment of burns, cut wounds, bruises, and as a pain reliever for conditions affecting bones, muscles, and joints. The oil is composed of approximately 70% unsaturated fatty acids. The primary component is oleic acid, which is a monounsaturated fatty acid. Additionally, emu oil contains about 20% linoleic acid (an Omega-6 fatty acid) and 1-2% linolenic acid (an Omega-3 fatty acid). There is some evidence to suggest that emu oil may have medicinal benefits. It is commonly applied topically to soften the skin and is often included in ointments designed to treat dry, cracked heels. Studies have demonstrated that emu oil can help reduce scar formation in healed burn wounds, as well as alleviate symptoms associated with muscle sprains and arthritis, due to its potent anti-inflammatory properties. Emu oil is classified as a completely neutral lipid because it lacks phospholipids. This unique characteristic allows it to penetrate the skin effectively.
